# A real DOI is not a verified claim: a SciFact and citation audit

Scientific reporting must distinguish existence, identity, publication status, entailment, and usage rights. We tested bibliographic metadata and a local model on expert-annotated claims.

![Study overview](/assets/research/ac07-cover.svg)

## Metadata is necessary, not sufficient

We queried six real DOIs and one fictional negative control through the [Crossref REST API](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/rest-api/). Five returned HTTP 200, one returned 429 and one returned 404. The real Centaur DOI was rate-limited, but its [publisher page](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09215-4) confirms existence. A 429 must remain unknown at that endpoint, not be treated as nonexistence. A retracted article was marked in its title while its update-to field was empty; the separate retraction notice linked the original DOI. See [Crossref's Retraction Watch documentation](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/retraction-watch/). A deliberately mismatched JITAI DOI resolved to a different paper. The correct DOI is [10.1007/s12160-016-9830-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12160-016-9830-8). Missing license metadata is not permission.

![Metadata request outcomes](/assets/research/ac07-metadata.svg)

## Testing claim verification

We pinned the [SciFact repository](https://github.com/allenai/scifact) to 68b98a56d93e0f9da0d2aab4e6c3294699a0f72e and downloaded the official data archive, recording file hashes. [SciFact](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.609/) has claims and annotations under CC BY 4.0, abstracts in an ODC-By 1.0 database, and Apache 2.0 code. Underlying text rights still need consideration.

From 5,183 abstracts and 300 public dev claims, we selected 36 unique claim IDs with cited documents supplied, 12 per class, restricting abstracts to at most 3,200 characters. Labels are SUPPORT, CONTRADICT and NEI (not enough evidence); the last is operationally assigned when the cited document has no evidence annotation. It does not mean a claim is false in the world. Local Qwen2.5:1.5b received the abstract and claim, at temperature zero with a JSON Schema. Retrieval, full text and rationale selection were not evaluated.

![Confusion matrix](/assets/research/ac07-matrix.svg)

All 36 outputs were valid and all predicted NEI. Accuracy was 12/36, or 33.33%, and macro F1 was 0.1667, no improvement over a constant-label baseline. A same-machine replay matched all recorded fields except elapsed time. There were 72 local calls and five tests passed under normal and optimized Python. Pretraining overlap is unknown; a small balanced public dev subset is not the official full benchmark. Indiscriminate abstention misses real supporting and contradicting evidence, despite valid output format.

## Adoption and limits

Record DOI, version, authors and dates, evidence spans, corrections and retractions, usage rights, retrieval time, and entailment separately. Retrieval failures are unknown, confirmed identity mismatches are mismatches. Full-text review, retrieval metrics, independent fresh claims and review remain in [issue #858](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-ops/issues/858). The result does not justify model promotion. Aggregate results and code only; no original claim/abstract corpus distributed. No Manager weights, production evaluator or app changed.

Attribution: Wadden et al. (2020), Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims; Crossref; Nature; Nahum-Shani et al. DOI 10.1007/s12160-016-9830-8. AI authorship: ChatGPT.
